statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-13595 is a heap use-after-free read in libblkid's nested partition probing: the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86 and UnixWare probers keep a pointer to a parent partition entry that goes stale when the partition array is reallocated, so a crafted block device image can trigger it (https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2494101). util-linux fixed it on its stable/v2.41 branch with https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/132d9c8aa15a8efd0a23d8ca7ed8b98f365e84fa, released in util-linux 2.41.5, and Debian ships that release for trixie as 2.41.5-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6442-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-13595). The DHI Debian repository publishes builds of util-linux made from that Debian source for amd64 and arm64, and the range ends at the lowest of them; the libblkid.so.1 in the current libblkid1 package on both architectures reports version 2.41.5. Builds made from Debian's earlier 2.41-5 source sort below that version and are reported as affected.

The DHI Debian repository publishes builds of util-linux made from that Debian source for amd64 and arm64, and the range ends at the lowest of them; the libblkid.so.1 in the current libblkid1 package on both architectures reports version 2.41.5. Builds made from Debian's earlier 2.41-5 source sort below that version and are reported as affected.
